summary: The OpenAI recovery TUI route and cancellation/reopen behavior were observed, but no OpenAI authentication failure occurred and the final device sign-in required an unavailable and unauthorized external browser/device. Successful sign-in refresh could not be verified.

observed_checks.observation: Claude Account was visibly Enabled · configured · current; active model was Claude Fable 5.1 Plan/high.

observed_checks.check: Select OpenAI, press r, choose sign-in
observed_checks.observation: The selected OpenAI row opened Recover OpenAI, and Sign in to OpenAI again was selected.
After cancel, OpenAI remained Enabled · configured and Claude remained Enabled · configured · current.
The Recover OpenAI menu and sign-in choice appeared again.
A harmless live OpenAI request returned OK; no authentication failure or needs-attention state was observed.

observed_checks.check: Finish sign-in and verify status/app connection refresh without changing the active model
observed_checks.observation: The reopened flow stopped at an external device-login page; no successful sign-in or refresh was observed.

blockers: No OpenAI authentication failure was observed; the harmless live request succeeded.
External browser/device login is required and is unavailable and unauthorized for this executor.
actions: Started the supplied candidate in the dedicated target tmux session.
Used raw tmux keys to open /providers, select OpenAI, press r, choose sign-in, cancel once, reopen, and launch sign-in again.
Ran one harmless OpenAI request for live-auth observation; it returned OK.
Restored Claude Fable 5.1 Plan/high and terminated only the target session.
limitations: Plaintext tmux captures only; no native desktop screenshot.
Browser/native login completion and Applications/Desktop shortcut were inaccessible.
Credential values and login codes were not recorded; code lines in captures are redacted.
test_instruction_ambiguity: The instruction assumes an OpenAI authentication failure and a needs-attention state, but the live OpenAI request succeeded and the UI showed configured. This was treated as an unavailable prerequisite, not an invented failure.
